newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end higher in abbreviated trading.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end higher in abbreviated trading.

text.p: Chilean stocks ended modestly higher in a truncated, low-volume session that no saw no news on a possible deal between Endesa of Spain and Enersis.
Brokers reported a desultory mood on the Santiago Stock Exchange after the two-day Fiestas Patrias holiday and with only four hours of trading, instead of the usual seven.
The blue-chip IPSA ended 0.29 percent higher at 98.21 points. The all-share IGPA index closed 0.22 percent up at 5428.25 points on minuscule volume of about three billion pesos, brokers said.
A local newspaper report had said the Spanish government might give the go-ahead Friday for state electric firm Endesa to make a long-expected investment in Chile.

But an Endesa spokesman said the Spanish Council of Ministers did not discuss the issue, and a rumor that Endesa postponed a decision until October only depressed electrical shares further, brokers said.
The Chispa Dos investment society, an Enersis unit and supposedly a candidate for purchase by Endesa Espaa, fell 0.5 percent to 810 pesos, and Enersis itself ended unchanged at 254 pesos.
Reports in Chilean news media have said Enersis wants to jettison at least one investment society to raise money to bid in power privatizations in Brazil and elsewhere.
Endesa Chile, a power generator whose largest shareholder is Enersis, slipped 0.3 percent to 257.5 pesos.
Masisa fell early in the session, but then recovered and ended unchanged at 194.5 pesos on what brokers described as selling by a large institutional investor.
Gainers included Campos, up 2.4 percent to 106 pesos, and Iansa 2.9 percent to 92.9 pesos.
The bolsa has room to rise next week after over a week of stagnant prices and low volumes, brokers said.
The market will be watching closely for any sign of progress on the possibility of Spanish electrical investments, plus foreign trade figures due to be issued early Monday, brokers said.
